correctness.rationale: The exact independent-chi-square representation and exact F moments yield moving endpoints with explicit first-order shifts. Taylor expansion of the conditional chi-square CDF in the normalized denominator uses exact central moments through order four; on a fixed neighborhood the derivatives are bounded and the complement is exponentially small. The endpoint algebra gives the signed coefficients \(\pm2\sqrt{2d}\,f_d(d\pm\sqrt{2d})\), so subtraction yields the positive coefficient and an \(O_d(m^{-2})\) remainder. The packaged numerical replay is corroborative only.

value.rationale: The source explicitly identifies higher numerator degrees as its obstruction. The new result determines the missing direction of approach to the chi-square endpoint for every fixed degree \(d\ge6\), with a closed positive first-order margin, and therefore proves a nontrivial sufficiently-large-denominator region of the conjecture for every such degree.
